15 Air is trapped inside a glass bulb which is immersed in water and attached to a U-tube containing
mercury. The densities of water and mercury are ρw  and ρm  respectively. The surface of the
water is open to the atmosphere where atmospheric pressure is P.

The acceleration of free fall is g.
What is the pressure of the air in the glass bulb?
A
P  +  gρwhw  +  gρmhm
B
P  +  gρwhw  –  gρmhm
C
gρwhw  +  gρmhm
D

hints: Notice where $h_w$ ends in the diagram - it is the vertical depth from the open water surface down to the level of the lower mercury surface on the left side.
Recall that pressure at a depth increases as $P + \rho g h$, so the water pressure at that lower mercury level is $P + g\rho_w h_w$.
Compare pressures at the same horizontal level in the mercury: the right mercury column is higher by $h_m$, so add $g\rho_m h_m$ to the bulb air pressure to balance the left-side pressure.
walkthrough: Identify the level where pressures can be equated: the horizontal dashed line through the lower mercury surface on the left. At the same level in a continuous fluid the pressure is the same.
Find the pressure on the left at that level. It is in water at depth $h_w$ below the surface open to atmosphere $P$, so $P_{left} = P + \rho_w g h_w$ using $\Delta p = \rho g h$.

Find the pressure on the right at that same level. The bulb air pushes on the top of the right mercury column, then there is an extra mercury column of height $h_m$ down to this level, so $P_{right} = P_{air} + \rho_m g h_m$.
Set $P_{left} = P_{right}$ for hydrostatic equilibrium: $P + g\rho_w h_w = P_{air} + g\rho_m h_m$.
Rearrange for the trapped air: $P_{air} = P + g\rho_w h_w - g\rho_m h_m$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Adds both liquid columns. The higher mercury on the bulb side means the air pressure is less than the water pressure at the lower mercury level, so the $g\rho_m h_m$ term must be subtracted.

B.explanation: Equating pressures at the lower mercury level gives $P + g\rho_w h_w = P_{air} + g\rho_m h_m$, so $P_{air} = P + g\rho_w h_w - g\rho_m h_m$.

C.explanation: Omits atmospheric pressure $P$. The water surface is open, so pressure at depth $h_w$ must include $P$ plus $g\rho_w h_w$.

D.explanation: Omits atmospheric pressure $P$. The water pressure at the mercury level is $P + g\rho_w h_w$, not only $g\rho_w h_w$.
